crm_notes: Account: large regional bank technology arm. Heavy regulatory constraints (data residency + audit trails).
Use-case prioritized: customer support assistant + document reranking for loan docs. Primary need: consistent latency for customer-facing chat (fast first-byte streaming).
AE notes (Maya): customer cares most about 95th percentile for short responses (<64 tokens) and 99th percentile for end-to-end conversations during peak batch jobs.
Customer quote: "We need predictable p95 under 150ms for quick chat replies; p99 we accept higher but require clear credit rules."
SE notes (Rafael): recommended Dedicated pool with mixed-instance sizing (8xA10G + 4xH100-style) to balance cost and burst headroom; evaluate KV cache hit rates and batching impact in POC.
Security feedback: will require on-prem deployment for production-critical flows and VPC for non-sensitive sandboxing. KMS integration mandatory.
Commercial: procurement prefers annual reserved commit, wants SLA with p95 target and explicit measurement method (client-side timing + server-side correlation).
Comparison: evaluated Vendor-A (cheaper) but failed residency tests; Vendor-B had better streaming metrics but no on-prem option. Redwood positioned on predictable dedicated + observability.

latency_slo_summary: Customer requires clear SLOs defined by request type: (1) short interactive chat (<=64 tokens): p50 < 40ms, p95 < 150ms, p99 < 350ms (first-byte streaming must be <120ms); (2) long generative responses (>512 tokens): p50 < 300ms, p95 < 1200ms, p99 < 2500ms (measured end-to-end); (3) batch reranking (embeddings + scoring): throughput target 3000 reqs/min with p95 < 200ms per item. Measurement: default is client-side wall-clock for SLA enforcement, with server-side traces used for diagnostics and credit disputes.
measurement_alignment: Define measurement anchors: client_first_byte, client_last_byte, server_receive_timestamp, server_send_timestamp.
Streaming SLOs anchored to first-byte visible to client (important for perceived latency); generation tail time tracked separately as 'completion latency'.
Non-streaming (sync) requests measured end-to-end (client send -> client receive).
All SLO windows use rolling 30-day aggregation for billing/SLA, 7-day rolling for operational alerts.
Warm-up and cold-starts: exclude first 5 minutes after node scale-up from SLA calculation; persistent cold-cache events must be documented and credited separately.
Synthetic load vs production: primary SLA measurement is production client-side timing; synthetic tests used for capacity planning and dispute replication only.
reserved_gpu_plan: Initial POC: 6 reserved GPUs (4 x A10G-equivalent for chat + 2 x H100-equivalent for high-throughput reranking). Target steady-state throughput: 1200 chat QPS with 95th <150ms for 64-token replies; headroom for 2x burst. Autoscaling policy: scheduled scale + manual burst for end-of-month peaks.
sla_negotiation_points: Explicit definition of measurement (client-side wall-clock) and list of excluded events (network provider outages, major cloud region outage).
Credits model: sliding credits tied to p95 breaches - customer requests graduated credit tiers at >0.5%, 1.0%, 2.0% monthly p95 breach levels.
Streaming first-byte vs completion: customer insists first-byte SLO be primary for chat; Redwood to provide per-stream metric reporting.
Maintenance windows: preferred maintenance windows and required 72h advance notice for major upgrades impacting inference kernels.
Data residency hard requirement for production flows; Redwood private deployment options need to be priced in.
